zh: (1903-50) an English writer of essays and novels. He was born in India and educated at Eton. His first job was with the British police in Burma (1922-7), but he reacted against his background and spent the next few years living with very little money in Paris and London. He wrote about his experiences among poor people there in Down and Out in Paris and London (1933). His next book, The Road to Wigan Pier (1937), described working-class life in Britain during the Depression. He joined the Republican side in the Spanish Civil War and wrote about this in Homage to Catalonia (1938). His two best-known novels, Animal Farm and Nineteen Eighty-Four, were written in the 1940s. In their different ways, they both show his disappointment with the results of socialist revolutions, especially in the Soviet Union.

zh: (1732-99) the first US President (1789-97), who had led its army to success in the American Revolution. He is called 'the Father of His Country'. The Continental Congress placed him in charge of the American forces in 1775. Although his army had a difficult and dangerous winter at Valley Forge, General Washington led them to several victories, including the final Battle of Yorktown. He later gave his important approval for the American Constitution and was elected in 1789 as the country's first president. He supported a strong central government but disliked political party arguments. He was elected a second time, but refused to stand as a candidate for a third time and returned to his home at Mount Vernon. Americans have always admired Washington as one of their best and most moral presidents. He is considered by many to have been the country's greatest leader and perhaps the only one who could have united the colonists during the American Revolution. Most people know the story of how as a boy he cut down his father's cherry tree and then admitted what he had done, saying, ‘I cannot tell a lie.’ The story may not be true but it is seen as a symbol of his honesty. Washington's fine personal qualities and fair politics were recognized during his life, and they seem even more impressive today. His memory is honoured by the Washington Monument and the names of the country's capital city, a state, many counties, government buildings, schools, streets, mountains, etc., and his image appears on the dollar note and the 25-cent coin.

觉察，察觉，识破（某人的不法行为）
开始讨论，转而谈论（新课题）
en: to contact somebody by phone, letter or email
ex: The heating isn't working; I'll get on to the landlord about it.
暖气不热，我得与房东联系一下。

zh: （谈及或问及工作情况）进展，进步
en: to have a friendly relationship with somebody
ex: She's never really got on with her sister.
她从未与妹妹真正和睦相处过。

en: to become known
ex: If this gets out there'll be trouble.
这事要是被人知道就麻烦了。

zh: 逃避，规避，摆脱（责任或义务）
en: to avoid a responsibility or duty
ex: We promised we'd go—we can't get out of it now.
我们答应过要去的，现在我们不能食言。

zh: 从疾病（或震惊、断绝关系等）中恢复常态
向（某人）讲清某事；让（某人）明白某事
完成，结束（令人不快但免不了的事）
en: to deal with or gain control of something
ex: She can't get over her shyness.
她无法克服羞怯心理。

zh: 别自以为是；别太当真了
en: to stop thinking that you are so important; to stop being so serious
ex: Just get over yourself and stop moaning!
别太当真了，停止抱怨吧！

zh: （常用讨好卖乖的手段）说服某人同意，哄骗某人依顺，笼络某人
en: to persuade somebody to agree or to do what you want, usually by doing nice things for them
ex: She knows how to get round her dad.
她知道怎样讨她爸爸的欢心。

en: to find the time to do something
ex: I meant to do the ironing but I didn't get round to it.
我本想熨衣服的，可就是抽不出时间。

zh: 帮助某人顺利通过考试
en: to use up a large amount of something
ex: We got through a fortune while we were in New York!
我们在纽约时花掉了一大笔钱！

zh: （尤指在努力帮助某人时）使某人理解，使某人接受（所讲的话）
en: to make somebody understand or accept what you say, especially when you are trying to help them
ex: I find it impossible to get through to her.
我发觉根本无法让她听懂。

en: to finish or complete a task

zh: 使烦恼；使生气；对某人产生影响
en: to annoy or affect somebody
ex: The pressure of work is beginning to get to him.
工作的压力使他烦恼起来。

en: to collect people or things in one place
ex: I'm trying to get a team together for Saturday.
我正设法召集一帮人过周六呢。

en: to stand up after sitting, lying, etc.
ex: The class got up when the teacher came in.
老师进来时全班起立。

en: to dress yourself/somebody as somebody/something else
ex: She was got up as an Indian princess.
她被打扮成了印度公主。

zh: 忙于，从事（尤指令人吃惊或不快的事）
en: to reach a particular point
ex: We got up to page 72 last lesson.
我们上一课学到第 72 页。

en: the beginning
ex: He's covered this case from the get-go.
他从一开始就报道此案。

zh: 回避（责任或义务）的办法；借口
en: a way of avoiding something, especially a responsibility or duty
ex: He said he'd come but he's looking for a get-out.
他说过他会来，但眼下他又在找借口。

en: an informal meeting; a party
ex: a family get-together at Christmas
一家人在圣诞节聚会

zh: （尤指奇特的）一套衣服，穿戴，装束
en: a set of clothes, especially strange or unusual ones
energy and a strong wish to get things done

zh: 短假；假日休闲地；适合度假的地方
en: an escape from a difficult situation, especially after committing a crime
ex: to make a quick getaway
迅速逃跑

zh: 花哨无用的物品；徒有其表的东西
en: an object that attracts attention but has no value or use

zh: （厨房或浴室的）煤气热水器，热水锅炉
（建筑物的）电热水器，热水锅炉
en: a natural spring that sometimes sends hot water or steam up into the air

zh: 女朋友（全写为 girlfriend，尤用于短信、电邮等）
en: (especially in text messages, on social media, etc.) girlfriend
